description: The pool: which items a channel's rules select from a library snapshot (docs/rules-format.md, Items and the pool, rules 1 to 5, with Sources, Exclusions, the rating ladder and String matching). A case has: name; libraries, the IDs of the libraries in the snapshot; items, the movies and episodes (id, kind 'movie' or 'episode', libraryId, seriesId, seasonId, productionYear, officialRating, genres, tags; seriesId, seasonId, productionYear and officialRating are null when the item has none); series, each series that an episode's seriesId points to and that is in the snapshot (id, officialRating, genres, tags); collections, each collection in the snapshot with the IDs of its member movies, episodes, series and seasons (a member that is itself a collection is not listed: collections are not followed); sources, exclusions and maxRating, as in a rules file (maxRating absent means no ceiling); and expected, the canonical IDs of the pool, sorted. The pool is a set: the order of items and of expected is not part of the rules. Fields that the pool does not read (runtime, dates, season and episode numbers) are left out; a test fills them with valid values. Counts are not part of the vectors. Names that are not ASCII are written as JSON escapes, so this file is all ASCII.
source: Expected values come from an independent Python reference written from docs/rules-format.md alone (Items and the pool rules 1 to 5, Sources, Exclusions, Maximum rating and the rating ladder, String matching), before the Kotlin evaluator in core:engine was read. It applies the rules as amended on 2026-10-19: exclusions fail closed (an exclusion naming a collection that is not in the snapshot empties the pool, and a genre or tag exclusion removes an episode whose series ID is set but whose series is not in the snapshot), and the rating ceiling checks an episode's series' rating too.

cases.name: rule 1: only movies and episodes count; a series, season or collection is never an item
rule 2 library: an item anywhere inside the library; other libraries do not match
rule 2 collection: a member movie
rule 2 collection: a member episode
rule 2 collection: an episode of a member series
rule 2 collection: a member season selects only its own episodes
rule 2 collection: every member kind together
rule 2 collection: a member that is itself a collection selects nothing (no recursion)
rule 2 collection: a collection absent from the snapshot as a source matches nothing
rule 2 series: every episode of that series, no movie, no other series' episodes
rule 2 series: the series is not in the snapshot, its episodes still match by ID
rule 2 genre: the item's own genre, or for an episode its series' genre
rule 2 genre: an episode of a series without the genre, a loose episode and an episode of a missing series use own names only
rule 2 tag: the item's own tag, or for an episode its series' tag
rule 2 genre: a movie takes a genre from itself only
rule 2 yearRange: the item's own year, both ends included; no year is not included; no guessing from the series
rule 2 yearRange: a single-year range
rule 3 union: an item matching several sources is in the pool once
rule 3 union: sources are a union, not an intersection
rule 3 exclusion genre: removes an item with the genre, and an episode whose series has it
rule 3 exclusion tag
rule 3 exclusion yearRange
rule 3 exclusion library: removes every item of that library
rule 3 exclusion series: removes the episodes of that series
rule 3 exclusion collection: removes a member movie and the episodes of a member season
rule 3 exclusions: several at once, any match removes
rule 3: a source equal to an exclusion contributes nothing; the exclusion wins
rule 3: an excluded item cannot be brought back by a second source
rule 3 fail closed: a collection exclusion whose collection is not in the snapshot empties the pool
rule 3 fail closed: an unresolved collection exclusion empties the pool even next to a resolved one
rule 3 fail closed: a collection exclusion that resolves removes only its members (control)
rule 3 fail closed: a genre exclusion removes an episode whose series is missing, whatever its own genres; a loose episode and a movie are checked on their own
rule 3 fail closed: a tag exclusion removes an episode whose series is missing
rule 3 fail closed: a library exclusion is decided by IDs and does not touch an episode of a missing series in another library
rule 3 fail closed: a series exclusion is decided by IDs and does not touch an episode of another missing series
rule 3 fail closed: a yearRange exclusion does not remove an episode of a missing series by that alone
rule 3 fail closed: a genre source uses an episode's own names only when its series is missing
rule 4 movie: passes only on its own rating, at or below the ceiling
rule 4 episode: own TV-Y7, series TV-MA, ceiling TV-Y7 is excluded (the stale rating triple)
rule 4 episode: series passes and own rating passes
rule 4 (a): an episode with no own rating takes its series' rating
rule 4 (a): an own rating of NR, blank or Unrated is used as it is, never replaced by the series' rating
rule 4 (b): a series rated NR, Unrated or blank blocks its episodes even with a passing own rating
rule 4 (b): a series with no rating, or the empty string, does not block; (a) decides
rule 4: a series above the ceiling blocks an episode whose own rating passes; a series at the ceiling does not
rule 4: an episode whose series is missing from the snapshot is not allowed under a ceiling
rule 4: a loose episode (no series ID) is checked on its own rating alone
rule 4: no ceiling admits everything, rated or not, even an episode of a missing series
rule 4: the ceiling is applied on top of sources and exclusions
rule 4: the ceiling Approved is rank 0
rules 3 and 4 together: a genre exclusion and a ceiling over an episode of a missing series
an empty result: sources that match nothing
an empty result: a snapshot with no items
an empty result: every item is excluded
string matching: ASCII letters fold in both directions
string matching: a trailing space is not trimmed from the server's name
string matching: a space in the rule's name is not trimmed either
string matching: NFC and NFD are different strings (the rule names NFC)
string matching: NFC and NFD are different strings (the rule names NFD)
string matching: non-ASCII letters match exactly, with no case folding
string matching: the Turkish dotted capital I (U+0130) and dotless i (U+0131) do not fold to i
string matching: a rule naming the Turkish dotted capital I matches only that
string matching: the Kelvin sign (U+212A) does not fold to k
string matching: a rule naming the Kelvin sign matches only it
string matching: a tag with an emoji (a surrogate pair in the file) matches by its code points
string matching: the same rules apply to exclusions
